title: “HOW WILL THIS BE?”
paragraphs: “HOW WILL THIS BE?”

Not rebellion.
Not unbelief.
Just an honest question from a trembling heart.
Nazareth was quiet that day.

No thunder.
No choir of angels filling the sky.

Just a young woman…
and a message that would fracture human history.
“Greetings, favored one.”
Mary’s world tilted.

She was not a queen.
Not a scholar.
Not a woman of power.
Just a village girl promised to a carpenter.
And then the impossible dropped into the room:

“You will conceive and give birth to a son…
and you will call His name Jesus.”
— Luke 1:31
Pause there.

Mary knew biology.
Mary knew culture.
Mary knew what pregnancy outside marriage meant in her village.

Shame.
Whispers.
Possible stoning.
So she asks the question every honest believer eventually asks:

“How will this be?”
— Luke 1:34
Notice something holy here.
She didn’t say “No.”
She asked how.

Faith is not the absence of questions.
Faith is bringing your questions to God instead of running from Him.
The angel answers:

“The Holy Spirit will come upon you…
and the power of the Most High will overshadow you.”
— Luke 1:35
Translation:
Mary, this miracle will not come from human strength.
It will come from God Himself.
Because the story of salvation has never depended on human ability.
Not Mary’s.
Not yours.
Not mine.
And then comes the moment that shakes heaven.
A teenage girl, staring at a future she cannot control, whispers the most dangerous prayer on earth:

“Behold, I am the servant of the Lord.
Let it be to me according to your word.”
— Luke 1:38
That sentence carried the weight of redemption.
Because the child in her womb would grow to carry another weight.
A cross.
Jesus would enter the world through Mary’s surrender…
and leave the world carrying our sin.

Your shame.
Your secret battles.
Your past you wish nobody knew.
All nailed to wood.
All buried in a borrowed tomb.
And three days later—
Resurrection.
So if you’re standing in a moment where God’s plan makes no sense…
If obedience feels risky…
If your heart whispers the same words Mary spoke—
“How will this be?”
Hear the quiet answer of heaven:

With God, nothing will be impossible.
— Luke 1:37

Not your restoration.
Not your forgiveness.
Not your new beginning.
Jesus specializes in impossible stories.
He is still rewriting them today.
Including yours.
Because the Gospel still turns questions into miracles.
And remember:
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
